lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: submitting and confirming receipt

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic submitting and confirming receipt task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Using a provided practice tracker for a fictional application (not a real account or real submission), the learner works through a submission-readiness checklist to confirm every required document is actually attached and complete, then drafts the message they would send afterward to confirm the application was received.
safetyNotes: No real application is submitted anywhere for this lesson and no real account or login is created; the deliverable is a completed checklist and a drafted follow-up message only.
The provided practice tracker uses a fictional applicant so the learner does not need to enter real personal or document details to complete the checklist.
materials: learner-local: the provided practice tracker for a fictional application
learner-local: paper or notes app for the drafted follow-up message

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Looking at your own tracker from earlier in this unit, which real item on it will need this same readiness check before you consider it truly submitted?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Readiness check accuracy: Readiness answer correctly identifies the missing second reference as blocking submission. | Follow-up message quality: Message names what was submitted, the submission date, and clearly requests confirmation. | Transfer to real tracker: Reflection names a specific real item and explains what readiness check it will need. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draft a second, different follow-up message for a scenario where two weeks have passed with no response at all, including how the tone and urgency should change from the first message.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using a provided practice tracker for a fictional application (not a real account or real submission), the learner works through a submission-readiness checklist to confirm every required document is actually attached and complete, then drafts the message they would send afterward to confirm the application was received.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact submitting and confirming receipt decision or action.
Model move 2: Before checking readiness, think about why 'I sent it' is different from 'I confirmed it arrived.'

Model move 3: Review the provided practice tracker (a fictional applicant's tracker showing: transcript attached, one of two references attached, personal statement attached, application fee status shown as 'waived').

Model check: Readiness check accuracy: Readiness answer correctly identifies the missing second reference as blocking submission. | Follow-up message quality: Message names what was submitted, the submission date, and clearly requests confirmation. | Transfer to real tracker: Reflection names a specific real item and explains what readiness check it will need.

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for submitting and confirming receipt.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using a provided practice tracker for a fictional application (not a real account or real submission), the learner works through a submission-readiness checklist to confirm every required document is actually attached and complete, then drafts the message they would send afterward to confirm the application was received.
Coach direction: Before checking readiness, think about why 'I sent it' is different from 'I confirmed it arrived.'
Learner prompt: Why might an application seem sent but not actually count as received or complete on the other end?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Review the provided practice tracker (a fictional applicant's tracker showing: transcript attached, one of two references attached, personal statement attached, application fee status shown as 'waived'). Work through the submission-readiness checklist against it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I checked that every required document type is present and marked complete, not just started.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I checked that document names/versions match what the application actually asks for (no placeholder or draft-labeled files).
Response 3 (t2-p3): Based on the practice tracker, is this fictional application actually ready to submit? If not, what specifically is missing?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Looking at your own tracker from earlier in this unit, which real item on it will need this same readiness check before you consider it truly submitted?

Success checks: Readiness check accuracy: Readiness answer correctly identifies the missing second reference as blocking submission. | Follow-up message quality: Message names what was submitted, the submission date, and clearly requests confirmation. | Transfer to real tracker: Reflection names a specific real item and explains what readiness check it will need.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: submitting and confirming receipt supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional submitting and confirming receipt condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Readiness check accuracy: Readiness answer correctly identifies the missing second reference as blocking submission. | Follow-up message quality: Message names what was submitted, the submission date, and clearly requests confirmation. | Transfer to real tracker: Reflection names a specific real item and explains what readiness check it will need..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
